q2_gaps: attributive kind-level adjective inside a predicate nominal ('a common garden ivy') — the adjective+noun rule offers only fusion into the compound or predication of the referent, while `KindProperty` is specified for copular predications of a kind
notes: `common` is one of `KindProperty`'s own listed properties and fails the 'could one individual be common?' test, so routing it there rather than onto the witness is well-supported even though the instruction set illustrates that head only for copular clauses. Fusing the whole phrase as a term-of-art plant name (`common_garden_ivy`) would have been the other rule-supported option.
